focus: Security and pinning hygiene across all 33 workflows
answeredQuestions: What security and pinning hygiene gaps exist in the workflows?

graphEvents.label: Dependabot write token exposed to fetch-metadata
Security work is 12 permission blocks plus guard

label: Action pinning is already complete: all 91 uses: references across the 33 workflows resolve to exactly five actions (actions/checkout x43, actions/setup-node x35, actions/setup-python x8, actions/upload-artifact x4, dependabot/fetch-metadata x1), every one a full 40-hex commit SHA with a trailing version comment; zero tag or branch refs and zero unpinned local/docker refs. Pinning is therefore not a remediation project but an invariant to lock with a guard test.

12 of 33 workflows declare no permissions: block and inherit the repository default token scope: advisory-checks, agent-mirror-sync, chart-corpus, comment-hygiene, diagram-corpus, markdown-link-integrity, playbook-operator-contract, prompt-card-sync, repo-rules-corpus, rule-canary-sync, runtime-no-spec-import, skill-doc-frontmatter. None performs a write (no git push/commit, no gh CLI, no GH_TOKEN), so this is a defense-in-depth and auditability gap, not an active write exposure; the fix is a uniform contents: read block in 12 files.

dependabot-auto-merge.yml grants contents: write and pull-requests: write at workflow level (lines 10-12), so the write token is also live during the third-party dependabot/fetch-metadata step, which is handed it explicitly via github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (lines 22-24); only the final gh pr merge --auto step (lines 36-40) needs contents: write. Because permissions are job-scoped, least privilege requires splitting a read-only metadata job from a write-scoped merge job, or at minimum a comment recording the accepted deviation. This is the one workflow whose token scope exceeds what each step needs.

The Dependabot auto-merge gate is sound against spoofing: it fires only on pull_request (never pull_request_target), the author test github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]' (line 18) reads server-set event data, the merge is further narrowed to npm_and_yarn plus npm-security or ungrouped plus semver-patch (lines 31-34), and gh pr merge --auto (line 40) defers the merge to branch-protection required checks. Residual risk is configuration-side only: nothing in the repository pins that required checks exist and cover the bumped paths, so a /doctor:ci audit should surface that dependency rather than the workflow YAML needing change.

The classic fork and secret attack classes are structurally absent: zero matches for pull_request_target and zero for workflow_run across all 33 workflows, and secrets.* appears in only two files - TRIGGER_INDEX_PUSH_TOKEN guarded by a '|| github.token' fallback (trigger-index-rebuild.yml:274) and secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN in dependabot-auto-merge.yml (lines 24, 36). No pull_request-triggered workflow reads a repository secret, and no workflow checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha, so a fork PR runs with a read-only token and no secrets.

No exploitable shell-injection path found. github.event.* reaches run: blocks in five workflows, but the only free-text field (the PR body) is deliberately routed through env: and written with printf '%s' (message-contract.yml:74 and 88-91, with an inline comment stating the reason), and direct ${{ }} interpolation inside run: source is limited to SHA fields (comment-hygiene.yml:25-26, agent-mirror-sync.yml:35-36, changed-packet-validation.yml:46-51) plus github.sha/ref_name/repository passed through env (message-contract.yml:48-51). Hex SHAs are not shell-injectable. The remaining issue is stylistic inconsistency - direct interpolation where env: is the house pattern - which sk-code-ci should codify as 'never interpolate expressions in run:, always env:'.

Only 6 of 33 workflows set timeout-minutes anywhere, so 27 can hold a runner for the 360-minute default when a test or network call hangs. This is the largest hygiene gap after permissions and belongs in the same standards pass: a per-job timeout-minutes is a one-line addition and the sk-code-ci review checklist should require it.

Answers the carried-forward question about hooks test scope: .skilled/hooks/vitest.config.ts:38 sets include to '<hooks root>/**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)', and line 19 filters out any path segment equal to node_modules. F3 (hooks test parallelism) therefore covers only tests physically under .skilled/hooks/, not the system-spec-kit runtime suite, so any fileParallelism change there cannot be credited with spec-kit test speedups.

Synthesis for the ranked recommendations: the security angle needs no remediation programme. It contributes three cheap, mechanical items - 12 one-line permissions: contents: read blocks, a two-job split of dependabot-auto-merge.yml, and timeout-minutes on the 27 workflows lacking it - plus one guard test that enforces four invariants (full-SHA pins, explicit read-only permissions, no pull_request_target/workflow_run, no secrets on pull_request). That guard belongs in the proposed sk-code-ci mode's review checklist and in /doctor:ci's audit surface, not in a new workflow.

Every action reference in .github/workflows resolves to a full 40-hex commit SHA; every workflow declares an explicit read-only permissions block unless a named job needs write; no workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run; no pull_request-triggered workflow reads a repository secret; every job declares timeout-minutes.

direction: Pull-request-target or fork-secret exploitation as the CI security driver
reason: Zero pull_request_target and zero workflow_run matches in 33 workflows; no secrets referenced by any pull_request-triggered workflow; no PR head SHA checkout.
